why: Many r/placestart and r/esperanto passages mix attack warnings with maintenance and repair, so the lead act decides.

why.T3-001: The room posts its own false April Fools headlines and replies play along, get fooled, or reveal the joke, rather than testing an outside claim.

why.T3-002: The item is mostly calls for the room's own members to come and place the Esperanto flag.
why.T3-015: Distinct passages gather the scattered flag talk into an official sticky thread, a planning mega thread, and a redirect to the existing thread.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-002's gate covers calls for hands but does not reach the official sticky megathread and redirection that gather the scattered calls into one planning place.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: T3-015 is satisfied by the official sticky, the mega thread for design planning, and the redirect of the flag call to the existing thread, supported by C0028837, C0259069 and C0920462.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: If forced to one, drop T3-015; the call for helpers remains, but the consolidation into one thread would be lost.

why.T3-005: Defence concepts lead, with calls to fight for the star, keep the T against red vandals, and warnings of attacks.
why.T3-006: Distinct passages call to remove, absorb, or attack r/counting as an offensive target.
why.T3-009: Distinct passages celebrate the finished design, thank helpers for finishing, and report that the flag survived to the end.

multiplacement_log.why_this_one: T3-006 is satisfied by the calls to remove or absorb r/counting and attack it from the right, supported by C0325389, C0991446, C0493647 and C0380953.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: If forced to one, drop T3-006; the defence of the star and flag remains, but the offensive removal of r/counting would be lost.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-005 covers defending the star and flag and T3-006 covers attacking Counting, but neither reaches the completed-design and survived-to-the-end celebration.
